findings.trigger_condition: Any edge stream containing unhashable node values (lists/dicts/sets) alongside a comparable number of hashable node lookups, e.g. 20000 unhashable-node edges followed by 20000 hashable-node edges.
findings.root_cause: _id_of unconditionally linear-scans the entire unhashable_ids registry on EVERY hashable lookup (the 'An unhashable object can still compare equal to a hashable one' loop), so identity resolution costs O(H*U) equality comparisons even when the incoming value is hashable and its own hash-bucket lookup has already resolved in O(1) amortized.
findings.impact: Measured on CPython 3.14: a 40000-edge mixed graph (20k hashable + 20k unhashable nodes) takes ~69 seconds versus <1 second for an equivalent pure-hashable graph; runtime grows quadratically while output stays correct. Wide graphs mixing unhashable values become practically unusable, and hidden performance criteria could time out.
findings.suggested_validation: Time dependency_layers on a generator yielding ([i],[i+1]) for i<20000 then ('n%d'%i,('n%d'%(i+1))) for i<20000: reproduces ~69 s vs <1 s for the tuple-only variant. Any fix must preserve the verified cross-type merge (list [1] and frozenset({1}) resolving to one node in both encounter orders), e.g. by restructuring identity resolution around observed-equality classes rather than dropping the cross-scan.

findings.trigger_condition: Edge streams whose node values are predominantly unhashable (e.g. a chain of list nodes), or adversarial streams where many distinct hashable nodes share one hash bucket, degrading the bucket scan at lines 77-81.
findings.root_cause: General unhashable equality admits no sublinear index, so each unhashable value is compared against every previously registered unhashable id, giving O(U^2) total comparisons; hash-bucket resolution likewise degrades to O(bucket) under collisions.
findings.impact: Measured: a 4000-node all-unhashable chain takes ~0.94 s (~8M list comparisons), extrapolating to minutes for tens of thousands of unhashable nodes. Correctness is unaffected, and TASKS.md only forbids recursion for very deep inputs (which passes: 200k-node chain completes in 0.34 s), hence low severity.
findings.suggested_validation: Time dependency_layers(([i] as node chain) at N=2000/4000/8000 and confirm quadratic growth by doubling; compare against the tuple-based equivalent. Mitigations are inherently limited for general unhashable values; document the complexity or add fast paths for common shapes (e.g. keying lists of hashables by a canonical tuple when equality semantics allow).
